entries.question: Can LinkML own Overcenter's structural ontology vocabulary without owning semantic truth?
entries.claim: On the corrected representative slice, LinkML projects one structural model with explicit built-in type imports, preserving tested scalar types while semantic identity remains an external invariant.
entries.contrast: Hand-maintain vocabulary and structural constraints independently across TypeScript, data contracts, documentation, and graph representations.
environment: Python >=3.10; hosted proof uses ubuntu-24.04 Python and records the resolved dependency set.
success_criteria: Schema and valid fixture validate while missing evidence and undeclared vocabulary fail.
Repeated JSON Schema and TypeScript generation is byte-identical; repeated SHACL generation is RDF-isomorphic even if Turtle ordering differs.
Generated JSON Schema and TypeScript preserve the tested string and boolean scalar types.
Renaming a modeled relation changes all three tested projections at their meaningful representation level.
A semantic-key mismatch remains structurally valid in LinkML and is rejected by an independent Overcenter semantic check.

artifacts: GitHub Actions run 35484865636: corrected exact-head LinkML ontology experiment passed 5/5; scalar fidelity, projection behavior, and the semantic-boundary negative control all passed.

entries.interpretation: A positive result supports LinkML only as structural vocabulary/projection tooling; semantic authority remains in deterministic Overcenter mechanisms.
non_claims: LinkML expresses Overcenter's temporal, transactional, evidentiary, or authority semantics.
LinkML belongs in the production runtime.
Generated TypeScript is a runtime validator.
Every generator preserves every source constraint.

entries.question: Can Overcenter maintain a reproducible total ordering of production-code importance from quantitative facts?
entries.claim: A revision-bound callable graph plus explicit authority/recovery semantics can derive an inspectable production-code criticality vector and a calibrated total order without ranking tests or experiments themselves.
entries.contrast: Periodically repeat a human ranking exercise or rely on generic complexity/hotspot metrics alone.
environment: Git with full repository history for revision-bound blame/change exposure
success_criteria: Only production callables under src/ enter the ranked population.
Configured authority and recovery selectors resolve exactly once.
The static graph is informative and unresolved internal calls are reported.
At least 80% of the initial pairwise calibration judgments agree.
Every surprising rank decomposes into quantitative vector components and graph evidence.
entries.interpretation: A production-only callable graph can derive a reproducible consequence order and a separate engineering-attention order from quantitative facts. At evaluated revision 737736d4bc799ceaa23190da1d2ff818507d2852 the production graph ranks 299 callables, resolves 84.5% of internal/unknown production calls, and agrees with 6/7 prior pairwise judgments. The lone reuse-over-identity disagreement remains evidence that callable granularity cannot represent every branch-level semantic claim. Exact-blob mutation evidence materially improves E, all 7 probes apply with 0 stale at the evaluated revision, and stale mutation evidence fails closed.
non_claims: Callable boundaries are the final semantic unit.
Static test reachability is equivalent to hostile-case evidence.
Exported-entrypoint reachability is equivalent to production telemetry.
The current weighting equation is uniquely correct.
